comments.author: @JasonPD-m9u
comments.text:
Friction and hysteresis are the big differences between simulation and reality. You can include friction in your simulation, but the amount of it that actually occurs in reality varies wildly based on factors like humidity, dustiness, and surface wear. Elastomeric materials like rubber often start out very grippy but get harder and less grippy over time. Some elastomers can get more sticky with time as they leach plasticizers (often apparent with old rubber dishwashing gloves). It doesn't matter how accurate your simulation is if the friction and hysteresis varies between parts or over time. 

If you look at the simulations of the walking tea kettle soft robot, you will note that its simulation doesn't match reality very closely. This would be even more evident if trying to simulate a robot that needs to handle mixed materials of varying age and cleanliness in a dirty environment like a typical factory or warehouse. 

I suppose a really smart software product might insert feedback loops any time friction or hysteresis is a factor? In that case, real world performance would depend on the sensor behavior matching the simulated sensor behavior.

We can’t just “let the robots do the work” under capitalism. The basic needs people require to SURVIVE are behind paywalls, which force anyone who isn’t already extremely wealthy (a ruling class capitalist generally) to sell themselves piecemeal, hour over hour, to one or another capitalist (at an inherently exploitative wage, less than the total value their labor produces, because otherwise there’s no profit in it for the capitalist) in order to obtain their basic needs & not rapidly decline/die, especially now that the capitalist class has essentially cut all the social safety nets out from under us & is chipping away at labor protections too (not to mention our civil rights, the existence of privacy, the ability to access a free & open internet, & so on). 

Automation (turbo-charged by AI) is eradicating the last remaining jobs that weren’t robotized or outsourced with the industrial/manufacturing base. Now they’re replacing service workers— even the creative jobs that in a hypothetical (removed from the context of the capitalist class hierarchy) automation is supposed to free humans up to spend their time on & enjoy… Instead, those jobs are all but disappearing, because capitalists typically don’t care that much about the quality/integrity of the art they use for advertising purposes, so if they can avoid paying a team of artists wages & instead just generate some AI slop in 2 seconds by typing a basic ass prompt then that’s what they’re often going to do, because every decision is made towards absolute profit maximization & any other consideration is systematically deemed an “externality” to be ignored… As things stand, it’s increasing tensions as this very real crisis accelerated without ANY consideration or how it’s impacting the tens of millions of people who are being thrust into basically chronic/permanent unemployment or underemployment. Capitalists are only driving wages lower & prices higher, & again they’ve eradicated the social democratic social safety nets that once existed, so this joblessness literally just leaves people on the street, starving, dying, in very short order. 

Now, I’m not saying that the technology is the problem. On the contrary, capitalism— the capitalist class hierarchy— is the problem; this 250 year old mode of production, descended from (or rather a more recent form of) the same class hierarchy that existed under feudalism & slavery, is antiquated, long out of date, & is providing fundamentally incompatible with the level of technological advancement we are at, & it’s destabilizing our entire social fabric, accelerating wealth inequality (which means increasing mass poverty as the norm, because practically 100% of the gains from rising productivity continue to go to the few major owners at the very top while the workers are excluded from those gains so severely that real wages continue to be suppressed into DECLINE despite average workers producing FAR more value than they used to decade over decade). It is the incompatibility between these extremely powerful productive technologies & a system in which they’re exclusively owned by a tiny minority elite of (disproportionately the ultrawealthiest) capitalists while almost everyone else is excluded & turned into increasingly desperate wage slaves with increasingly few job opportunities that is the problem. And it’s not a hard choice which to reject— capitalism is also denying us democracy, leading to the rise of fascism & neo-feudalism as the ruling class grow more & more desperate to keep the masses powerless, marginalized, & complacent as the contradictions inherent in the system grow more in-our-faces & unmistakable every day… I’ve been pointing it out for ~16-17 years now, since I was a young teenager, & others have been pointing it out since capitalism has existed, since Marx & Engels & Proudhon & Kropotkin & the like. But by now, when there are just 5-10 individuals with HUNDREDS OF BILLIONS EACH in personal wealth (not to speak of the trillions embodied in corporations they largely autocratically control), 3,000 billionaires worldwide, & that small number control almost all the wealth, resources, & institutions while the other 8 billion of us are largely left to rot, bombarded with propaganda & indoctrination to convince us that capitalism isn’t the problem, to scapegoat anyone from immigrants & refugees to labor organizers & the left to Muslims, LGBTQ people, Chinese workers, Mexican workers— whoever they can point at to distract us from those who actually make the policies that devastate us, profit from suppressing our wages, profit from crushing unions, profit from price gouging, profit from shredding regulations intended to protect us from them (as consumers & as workers), profit from the wars they send poor people to kill & die in, profit from the fossil fuels that are leading towards the collapse of human civilization… And ultimately, while some very bad people disproportionately rise to the top in hierarchies that reward people for behaving in harmful, anti-human ways, the reality is that the systemic problem isn’t the people— it’s the class hierarchy. It’s the system that incentivizes & rewards everyone (whether they’re a legit sociopath/psychopath or not) for behaving sociopathically— ignoring the social, human, ecological, & macroeconomic consequences of their actions in favor of whatever maximizes profit regardless of the cost to others. 

Now, we could abolish the class divide & have a free & democratic society in which “those who work in the mills/factories/etc., own them,” in which our tax revenues & public resources could be directed towards the rational aims of dealing with the systemic crises that face us (like climate catastrophe) & meeting all human need first & foremost instead of letting capitalist middle men skim tens or hundreds of billions off the top while many of us go hungry, homeless, are deprived of health care, & so on, while they buy out any semblance of representative (let alone democratic) government… We could reject fascism AND the plutocratic neoliberal capitalist status quo & take the path to genuine, full universal emancipation. And in that kind of world, productive technologies (owned equally by each of the workers who use them to produce at a firm) would actually serve us again instead of enslaving us. In that kind of world, the massive revenues these technologies allow us to generate could actually go to everyone, without anyone being left out, & rather than 1 accumulating $200 billion at the cost of tens of millions living in destitute poverty, we could ALL enjoy a high standard of living at the minimum baseline, we could all work far shorter work hours (the only reason we can’t now is because [a] people NEED to work obscenely long hours of 50-80+ hours a week just to make ends meet when their wages are $7.25 an hour, or $10 an hour, with costs of living as high as they are, & [b] the profit motive incentivizes capitalists to squeeze the longest hours out of us that they can get away with, & it’s only when the labor movement has intervened to demand a limit that, briefly, we had a maximium 40 hour work week under New Deal social democracy)… 

If we abolished capitalism, we really could just “let the machines do the work—“ at least the undesirable labor that humans don’t WANT to do, freeing us up to focus on what really matters in truly utopian fashion. And that’s when you get to notions of “fully automated luxury communism.” That at a certain point, if we achieve a post-work society, & produce enough to create a post-scarcity economy, then markets become obsolete, currency becomes obsolete, people can largely just have what they want/need within reason & focus their lives on things more meaningful than just material acquisition for material acquisition’s sake… Self-development, philosophy, science, the arts, passion projects… But forget that kind of utopian goal for the time being— we would be in an INFINITELY better situation if we were simply liberated from the class hierarchy & the total domination of our society by a handful of multi-billionaire capitalists, including literal Nazis/fascists & Nazi/fascist sympathizers. If the profit motive wasn’t driving us off a cliff & we could actually address climate change, that alone would drastically shift the trajectory of the future for the better— from a rapid decline into fascism & ultimately extinction, to an ascent into utopia & perhaps even a realistic shot at proliferating into the solar system or even the stars (which, even if Elon Musk or whoever achieved it under capitalism, which is looking very unlikely, it would be less like a Star Trek-like ideal future & more like the galaxy being infected with a cancer… I mean, a billionaire’s privately owned pro-Nazi empire expanding across the galaxy sounds like some 40K nightmare whir I would never want to actually come to pass, but thankfully he’s 75% lies to investors & overpromises on things he lacks the intelligence or know-how to deliver upon, & 25% too busy trying to profit off our tax dollars every way he possibly can while spreading Nazism on Earth, so the rest of space is probably safe for the time being).
